tagline: Brazilian state-controlled oil and gas exploration, production, refining and marketing company
hero_kpi_rationale: Petrobras' sales revenues are the primary performance indicator reflecting its production and sales volumes of oil, gas and refined products. It is essential for assessing the company's overall performance in the energy sector, influenced by global oil prices and production volumes.

kpis.name: Sales revenues
kpis.explanation: Total amount of sales of products and services of the company.
kpis.description: Sales revenues represent the total amount generated from the company's core activities, including exploration, production, refining and marketing of oil and gas.
kpis.signal: Slight decline in sales revenues, impacted by oil prices and volume.

kpis.name: Gross profit
kpis.explanation: Difference between sales revenue and cost of goods sold.
kpis.description: Gross profit indicates the profitability of core operations before accounting for other operating expenses and financial charges.
kpis.signal: Gross margin is decreasing, reflecting higher production costs or lower selling prices.

kpis.name: Research and development expenses
kpis.explanation: Costs incurred for research and development of new products or technologies.
kpis.description: R&D expenses represent costs incurred for research and development. They are crucial for innovation and long-term competitiveness in the energy sector.
kpis.signal: Increase in R&D investments, potentially for innovation or energy transition.

kpis.name: Finance debt
kpis.explanation: Total amount of debt incurred by the company.
kpis.description: Finance debt represents the company's borrowings (2,186 M$ short-term + 24,255 M$ long-term according to the balance sheet as of 12.31.2025), composed of short- and long-term bonds.
kpis.signal: Significant increase in finance debt, requiring monitoring of repayment capacity.

kpis.name: Total Employees
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees of the company.
kpis.description: Total employees is an indicator of the company's size and human resource needs.
kpis.signal: Data not available in the provided text.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures

kpis.description: Capital expenditures are essential for growth and maintenance of production infrastructure, particularly in the oil and gas sector.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale.

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions.
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends + buybacks (2021-2025) in billions USD. Source yfinance cashflow.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du résultat net redistribuée. >80 % = potentiellement non soutenable.

kpis.name: Net Capitalized Costs O&G
kpis.explanation: Coûts bruts capitalisés pour les activités d'exploration et production pétrolière, nets des amortissements cumulés.
kpis.description: Net capitalized costs reach $143.7 Bn in 2025, up from $115.5 Bn in 2024, reflecting a significant acceleration in investments in oil and gas assets. This increase reflects the intensification of Petrobras' development program.

kpis.name: O&G Development Costs
kpis.explanation: Montant total engagé pour le développement des réservoirs prouvés, incluant les dépenses capitalisées et passées en charges.
kpis.description: Oil development costs stand at $16.8 Bn in 2025, up nearly 20% versus 2024, confirming the strategy to expand production capacity. The uptrend has been continuous since 2023.

kpis.name: Proved Oil Reserves
kpis.explanation: Volume total de réserves pétrolières prouvées (développées et non développées) estimées selon les définitions SEC.
kpis.description: Total proved reserves reach 10.1 billion barrels at end-2025, driven by positive revisions of 1.32 billion barrels. Steady reserve growth over three years strengthens long-term production visibility.

kpis.name: Depreciation & Amortization O&G
kpis.explanation: Charge de dépréciation, épuisement et amortissement liée aux actifs d'exploration et de production pétrolière.
kpis.description: The DD&A charge on oil and gas operations jumps to $11.7 Bn in 2025, reflecting the ramp-up of the capitalized asset base. This increase mechanically compresses operating results from extractive activities.

kpis.name: Oil & Gas Operations Result
kpis.explanation: Résultat net des activités d'exploration-production après impôts, hors frais de siège et charges d'intérêts.
kpis.description: Oil and gas operations result stands at $17.2 Bn in 2025, down 7.3% versus 2024 and significantly below the $22.5 Bn peak in 2023. Rising production costs and amortization charges weigh on profitability despite stable revenues.

ai_positioning.summary: Petrobras, operating in the oil and gas sector, shows no indication of integration or strategic positioning related to artificial intelligence in the provided documents. The activities and investments described are focused on exploration, production, refining and marketing of fossil fuels.
